title: Energy-Descent Reasoning vs Autoregressive Baseline (the Kona premise test)
task_name: GSM8K (original questions, exp281 corpus), held-out shuffled split
compute_parity_note: Both conditions use the same base model unsloth/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-GGUF (Qwen3.6-35B-A3B MoE, ~3B active params, Q4_K_M) on the same 200 paired problems. AR baseline = 1 greedy generation/problem. Energy-descent = 3 sampled generations/problem (temp 0.8) + 8 latent gradient-descent steps under a frozen FoVer-trained Boltzmann-GPT energy (16-dim, negligible FLOPs). Energy-descent therefore spends 3x the generation budget of the greedy AR baseline; the equal-compute AR control (self-consistency majority vote over the same 3 samples) scored 0.8950. Read the headline delta against ar_baseline_accuracy for the literal AR comparison and against self_consistency_accuracy for the equal-budget comparison.
